proof.text: Recover CompactSpace and QuasiSeparatedSpace for the source S by induction on the actual tree path: every vertex tree carries both instances. Apply the source kernel-generation lemma to obtain (ker u)[0] in G_S.

Apply support-path preservation to get J(ker u)[0] in G_X. Separately prove by path induction that J is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits. Open edges use the existing exact extension-by-zero instances; closed edges use closedSupport_lowerStarExact with the displayed complementary open sibling.

Form the actual short complex ker(u) -> L -> image(u), with second arrow factorThruImage u. Mathlib exact_kernel(u).isColimitImage identifies the second arrow as the cokernel of the first, giving a short exact sequence. Map it by exact J and form its singleTriangle. For any admissible class P, J(ker u)[0] lies in P by the preceding steps and JL[0] is a defining generator. ObjectProperty.ext_of_isTriangulatedClosed₃ on the distinguished triangle gives J(image u)[0] in P. Quantifying over P is exactly the required hull membership.

title: Derived generation of supported images by finite scalar local models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A support chain over $X$ is a finite chain $S=X_r\xrightarrow{a_r}\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}X_0=X$, each arrow a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Set $J=(a_1)_!\cdots(a_r)_!$, where at a closed arrow the notation $(a_k)_!$ means the ordinary closed direct image $(a_k)_*$; the empty chain gives the identity [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. A finite scalar local model on a scheme $V$ is a $\Lambda_V$-module which on each member $U_i$ of some pro-étale cover is $\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline\Lambda}\underline{P_i}$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda$-module $P_i$. Both underlines mean discrete constant sheaves, and the scalar modules may vary with $i$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Let $\mathcal G_X$ be the intersection of all full replete classes of objects of $D(\mathcal A_X)$ with the following properties. They contain zero and $JL[0]$ for every support chain and finite scalar local model $L$ on its source; they are closed under integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions, and retracts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. A retract means maps $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $pi=\mathrm{id}_K$. They are closed under all small products in the derived category [def-weil-category-product]. Finally, whenever $I$ is a small filtered category and $C_i^\bullet$ is a strict diagram of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-modules with a common termwise lower bound and every $Q(C_i^\bullet)$ in the class, the class contains $Q(\varinjlim_i C_i^\bullet)$, where the colimit is termwise in module sheaves and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This paragraph is the explicit meaning of $\mathcal G_X$, not an appeal to an unspecified closure convention.

For every support chain over $X$ and every actual module morphism $u:L\to M$ between finite scalar local models on its source, one has
$$J(\operatorname{im}u)[0]\in\mathcal G_X.$$
The image is the abelian module-sheaf image. Covers and scalar modules for $L,M$ may differ, and the maps may have arbitrary continuous matrix entries. This includes integral torsion local models. No closed pair, cohomology comparison, torsion-rigidity assumption, Noetherianity, cohomological-dimension bound, or finite-subextension-valued restriction is assumed. Empty schemes, zero coefficient rings, zero maps, identity maps and empty support chains are included.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q120-fdcbab345 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, and Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach (HRS) Ex 3.6, Lem 4.1, Ex 4.2, Prop 4.3 with (4.2), Cor 4.7, Rem 6.4 and Thm 6.12. This is a first split: the base item was unsplit, so the re-split rule does not apply, and the statement is unchanged. Steps: (1) Every member of the chain is qcqs. sk-thm-pe-weakly-contractible-basis gives w-contractible affine charts, and projectivity of h_U gives the weakly-contractible hypothesis of the descent node. The step says 'weakly contractible' where the basis theorem gives w-contractible; harmless. (2) lem-sfb-wcontractible-component-derived-hom gives F_W exact and fully faithful and π_0(W) extremally disconnected. Exact pullback of the matrix presentation gives F_W(B_R)=Λ_W⊗B. Degree-0 Hom equals module Hom, so v is a module map, and b^*K≅F_W ker v. (3) The evaluation node and det-pe-sections-conservative(3) show that F_W preserves sheaf products. det-pe-products-derived plus full faithfulness then identifies the source derived product. Colimits, shifts, triangles and retracts are fine. (4) The inverse class is admissible, so H_P⊆F_W^{-1}G_W, and node 1 applies. (5) The descent node's hypotheses are met. (6) j_! preserves products (det-sf-open-closed-extension-zero-limits(2), qcqs target) and colimits as a left adjoint. i_* preserves filtered colimits (lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed, qcqs target) and products as a right adjoint. So J(G_S)⊆G_X. (7) The image short exact sequence gives a triangle whose cone is J(im u)[0]. New nodes: both are statement-only and self-contained, with the closure class written out, and neither restates a clause of the item. For node 1 I tested empty and singleton P and finite discrete Λ (locally constant matrices). The critical case is the HRS Ex 4.2/Rem 6.4 βN kernel, which is not lisse but is in the hull: over Z_ℓ it is fib(R→∏_n e_{n}R), and over Q_ℓ a bounded colimit of that. HRS Thm 6.12 (C(S,Λ) semi-hereditary) supports plausibility; I found no false case. Node 2 is a plausible Čech/Rlim descent and passes the small cases (identity cover, empty V, zero N). Duplicate search: norm-local-model-finite-field-derived-generation, integral-continuous-cokernel-local-model, profinite-constant-derived-functions, local-model-cohomology-descent and principal-complete-heart-kernels all differ. Batch 5: lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site reaches def-trf-geometric-morphism, a plain definition of geometric morphisms. The w-contractible component nodes reach lem-trf-geometric-inverse-image-exact, which is Stacks 04JC exactness of inverse image, a general topos fact. Neither is a trace-formula or Poincaré-duality step, and both arrive through existing nodes, so I accept all four flags. The generic tool_uses are accepted. No fixes.
